## Q1
If the total number of applications received in Jan 2025 were double the number of applications received in Feb 2025, then the applications received under the area 'Others' in Feb 2025 were how much percent of the applications received under the same area in Jan 2025?

A firm provides consultancy in various areas — Education, Finance, Health, Social Media, Marriage and Others — on the basis of applications received. The table gives, for each area, the percentage of that month's applications during 2025. The total number of applications received during Feb 2025 was larger than the number received in Apr 2025, and the total received during Jan 2025 was larger than the number received in Mar 2025.

| Area (% of month) | Jan | Feb | Mar | Apr |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Education | 38 | 33 | 19 | 17 |
| Finance | 25 | 30 | 37 | 45 |
| Health | 11 | 18 | 5 | 18 |
| Social Media | 5 | 3 | 10 | 6 |
| Marriage | 3 | 7 | 10 | 11 |
| Others | 18 | 9 | 19 | 3 |
| Total | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% |

## Q1 - Options
(A) 200%
(B) 100%
(C) 50%
(D) 25%

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Data Interpretation
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q1

Suppose the February total is F applications; then the January total is double, namely 2F. The area 'Others' accounts for eighteen percent of applications in January, which works out to 0.18 times 2F, that is 0.36F applications. In February 'Others' accounts for nine percent, which is 0.09F applications. Expressing the February figure as a fraction of the January figure gives 0.09F divided by 0.36F, which equals one quarter, or 25 percent.

## Q3

## Q7
Which of the following, taken together, make a valid syllogism?<br>
A. Apples are not sweets.<br>
B. Some apples are sweets.<br>
C. All sweets are tasty.<br>
D. Some apples are not tasty.<br>
E. No apple is tasty.<br>
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q7 - Options
(A) B, D, C only
(B) E, A, B only
(C) C, E, A only
(D) C, B, E only

## Q7 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Logical Reasoning (Venn, Syllogism, Arguments)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q7

Take 'All sweets are tasty' (C) and 'No apple is tasty' (E). If any apple were a sweet it would have to be tasty, contradicting E; hence no apple is a sweet, i.e. 'Apples are not sweets' (A). So C and E validly yield A. The other groupings mix particular and negative premises that do not produce a valid conclusion.

## Q16

## Q18
Match List-I with List-II.<br>
Choose the correct answer from the options:

| List-I (Letter series) | List-II (Missing letter) |
|---|---|
| A. Q, N, K, H, E, ?<br>B. O, B, L, ?, I, D, F, E, C<br>C. Z, U, Q, N, L, ?<br>D. A, C, ?, G, I | I. C<br>II. K<br>III. B<br>IV. E |

## Q18 - Options
(A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
(B) A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
(C) A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III
(D) A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV

## Q18 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Mathematical Reasoning (Series, Coding, Relationships)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q18

A: Q, N, K, H, E step down by 3, so the missing term is B (III). C: Z, U, Q, N, L decrease by 5, 4, 3, 2, so the next is K (II). D: A, C, ?, G, I step up by 2, giving E (IV). B resolves to the missing letter C (I). Hence A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

## Q19
A computer costs 50,000 rupees and a printer costs 20,000 rupees. In a sale the price of the computer is reduced by 17% and that of the printer by x%. If a person purchased both the printer and the computer for a total of 50,000 rupees, then the value of x is:

## Q19 - Options
(A) 57.5
(B) 52.5
(C) 33
(D) 66

## Q19 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Mathematical Aptitude (Arithmetic)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q19

Reducing the computer price by seventeen percent leaves eighty-three percent of fifty thousand, which is forty-one thousand five hundred rupees. Since the person spends fifty thousand rupees altogether, the amount left for the printer is fifty thousand minus forty-one thousand five hundred, that is eight thousand five hundred rupees. The printer originally cost twenty thousand, so the reduction is eleven thousand five hundred rupees, and dividing that reduction by the original twenty thousand gives zero point five seven five, meaning the printer discount x equals fifty-seven point five percent.

## Q22
Match List-I with List-II.<br>
Choose the correct answer from the options:

| List-I (Broken Rule) | List-II (Associated Fallacy) |
|---|---|
| A. Middle term undistributed in the premises.<br>B. Presence of two negative premises in an argument.<br>C. Particular conclusion with negative premises.<br>D. Any term distributed in the conclusion but undistributed in the premises. | I. Existential Fallacy<br>II. Fallacy of illicit major and minor term<br>III. Exclusive premises<br>IV. Undistributed Middle |

## Q22 - Options
(A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
(B) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
(C) A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
(D) A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

## Q22 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Logical Reasoning (Venn, Syllogism, Arguments)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q22

An undistributed middle term is the fallacy of Undistributed Middle (IV). Two negative premises is the fallacy of Exclusive Premises (III). Drawing a particular conclusion where the premise structure does not support existence is the Existential Fallacy (I). A term distributed in the conclusion but not in the premises is the fallacy of illicit major/minor term (II). Hence A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

## Q27

| List-I | List-II (Interval) |
|---|---|
| A. All real x satisfying (4x + 1) &lt; 13 and (x + 1) &gt; 3<br>B. All real x satisfying 1 ≤ (x² + 1) &lt; 5<br>C. All real x satisfying (x + 7) &lt; (3x + 1) &lt; (x + 9)<br>D. All real x satisfying 5 &lt; (4x − 15) &lt; 9 | I. (5, 6)<br>II. (3, 4)<br>III. (2, 3)<br>IV. (−2, 2) |

(A) A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

**Answer:** A

**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q27

For item A, the first inequality gives x less than three and the second gives x greater than two, so the solution interval is from two to three, which is option three. For item D, adding fifteen and dividing by four gives x between five and six, which is option one. Hence the matching is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

## Q32

B. True discount on a present worth of 8000 for 3 months at 8% per annum<br>
C. True discount on a present worth of 6000 for 6 months at 6% per annum<br>

E. True discount on a present worth of 9000 for 6 months at 5% per annum<br>
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q32 - Options
(A) C &lt; A &lt; D &lt; B &lt; E
(B) A &lt; B &lt; D &lt; E &lt; C

(D) A &lt; B &lt; D &lt; C &lt; E

## Q32 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Mathematical Aptitude (Arithmetic)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q32

## Q46
As per the passage, disability can be done away with by:

Perhaps the best known of these sociologists is Oliver (1990), who argues that the biomedical model of disability leads to what he calls an ideology of personal tragedy which stresses the need for the individual disabled person to come to terms with 'their' problem, by struggling to cope as best they can.

Oliver calls this the personal tragedy model because it tends to describe disability as some terrible personal problem, which has ruined that person's life. He suggests that this model has now become taken for granted, achieving 'ideological hegemony' in the way that disabled people are viewed.

In place of the individualistic or personal tragedy model, Oliver argues that disability should be seen as a social problem and that it can only be understood within a wider social and economic framework, that is, within a social model.

Oliver argues that a clear distinction can be made between impairment and disability. A person may have a physical impairment of some kind, but it only becomes a disability when society organises social and economic features in such a way as to translate the impairment into a disability. For example, if the only means to enter a cinema is by using steps, then a person who has an impairment which leads them to use a wheelchair becomes disabled. However, if a ramp is provided and the ticket booth is at a lower height, and adequate spaces are provided for wheelchair users, then the person is no longer disabled. So, disability derives from organising society in such a way as to change impairment into disability.

## Q46 - Options
(A) Giving adequate medical treatment to everyone.
(B) Reorganizing society to facilitate access of all social space to the impaired.
(C) Re-orienting disabled persons.
(D) Re-orienting parents to prevent the birth of disabled children.

## Q46 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Comprehension
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q46

Oliver's social model holds that disability is produced when society is organised so that impaired people cannot use social spaces; therefore removing those barriers — ramps, lower counters, adequate space — removes the disability. Medical treatment (A) and 're-orienting' disabled persons or parents (C, D) target the individual, which is exactly the personal-tragedy view Oliver rejects.
